title: Scalar localization internal-Hom comparison with every telescope leg and evaluation
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], $A$ a commutative ring, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings with a map $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,R)$, and $t\in A$. Use the specified scalar actions [def-weil-pbc-scalar-localization-coefficient-actions], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their ordinary unbounded derived categories with localization functors $Q_R,Q_S$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and assume filtered colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Put $S=R[1/t]$, the sheafified sectionwise localization with underlying module the repeated-$t$ telescope [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization, def-weil-pbc-ringed-site-section-localization]. Write $F=S\otimes_R^L-$, $U$ for derived restriction, and $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to UF$ for their unit [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars, lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Write $H_R,H_S$ for ambient derived internal Hom with evaluation $\operatorname{ev}$ and relative derived tensor [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pc-kflat-complex].

Suppose $K\in D(R)$ has the following continuity property: for every sequential diagram $(M_n^\bullet)$ with a common termwise lower bound, the evaluation-induced map $\varinjlim_n H_R(K,M_n^\bullet)\to H_R(K,\varinjlim_n M_n^\bullet)$ is an isomorphism, with exact termwise sheaf colimits of functorial representatives [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $L\in D(R)$ have cohomology zero in sufficiently negative degrees. Let $\chi:F H_R(K,L)\to H_S(FK,FL)$ be the transpose of scalar-extended evaluation, and let $\rho:UF H_R(K,L)\to H_R(K,UFL)$ be its restriction followed by the scalar adjunction normalized by precomposing restricted evaluation with $K\to UFK$ [lem-sfb-dc-hom-scalar-adjunction].

For a complex $C$, let $T_t(C)$ be its constant sequential diagram with transition multiplication by $t$, let $j_n:C\to\operatorname{colim}T_t(C)$ be its legs, and put $\lambda_n(T)=t^{-n}\eta_T:T\to UFT$. For every pair of complexes $C_H,C_L$ with isomorphisms $e_H:Q_RC_H\simeq H_R(K,L)$ and $e_L:Q_RC_L\simeq L$, there are isomorphisms
$$\beta_H:Q_R(\operatorname{colim}T_t(C_H))\simeq UFH_R(K,L),\quad
\beta_L:Q_R(\operatorname{colim}T_t(C_L))\simeq UFL,$$
whose composites with $Q_Rj_n$ are respectively $\lambda_n(H_R(K,L))\circ e_H$ and $\lambda_n(L)\circ e_L$. There is an isomorphism
$$\gamma:Q_R(\operatorname{colim}T_t(C_H))\simeq H_R(K,Q_R(\operatorname{colim}T_t(C_L)))$$
satisfying
$$H_R(K,\beta_L)\circ\gamma=\rho\circ\beta_H,\qquad
\gamma\circ Q_Rj_n=H_R(K,Q_Rj_n\circ e_L^{-1})\circ e_H.$$
These are the canonical evaluation-induced continuity maps, compatible with quasi-isomorphic changes of representatives; neither $C_H$ nor $C_L$ is required to be termwise bounded below. Finally the following equality of morphisms in $D(R)$ holds for every $n\geq0$:
$$\operatorname{ev}_{K,UFL}\circ((\rho\circ\lambda_n(H_R(K,L)))\otimes\mathrm{id}_K)
=\lambda_n(L)\circ\operatorname{ev}_{K,L}.$$
Thus the stage pairing is $t^{-n}$ times scalar-extended evaluation, including for $n=0$. No completeness, constructibility, or perfectness is assumed beyond the displayed continuity property and the cohomological lower bound on $L$.

proof.text: Use the already proved localizationComplexCocone, its IsColimit proof, localizationUnderlyingDerivedIso, and localizationUnderlyingDerivedIso_unit in the existing internal-Hom localization module. The scalar defined by the coefficient action is definitionally localizationComplexScalar for the section a(t). The unique colimit isomorphism therefore identifies the actual repeated-t colimit with this model, and its localized zeroth leg is exactly the specified derived adjunction unit. These are proved private helpers accessed by a proof-only import all; no public interface is changed. Standard small-site coefficient instances are reused directly from RationalTermHom.coefficientSheafify, RationalTermHom.coefficientCompose and RationalTermHom.coefficientLocallyBijective; no duplicate cache theorems are introduced.

Compute restriction of the localized coefficient algebraMap(r) on module sheaves using scalarLocalizationCoefficientMap and its lift equation. Naturality of exact derived restriction factors transports this identity through Q and then through an arbitrary representative isomorphism. In particular multiplication by t on every UFT is invertible, with inverse supplied by invSelf(t). The inverse-scalar successor calculation gives t times lambda_(n+1) = lambda_n.

For each representative e:QP ≅ T define beta_P as the colimit identification of step 1 followed by UF(e). Its zeroth-leg equation is unit naturality. Induction on n, cancelling multiplication by t on UFT and using the two successor equations, proves every leg equation. The existing localizationDerivedRestriction_full and adjunction Hom equivalence show that maps from UF(QP) into a restricted localized object agree if they agree after the unit. Apply this to the beta maps for a chain map: the zeroth-leg square is the ordinary colimit-map equation and the assumed compatibility of e and e'. This gives the presentation change equation, with no boundedness on P.

Use the existing localizationHomComplex_transition and localizationHomResolutionIso_naturality: conjugating their scalar equality gives H(K,t id_QP)=t id_H(K,QP). Transport along QP ≅ T to get it for every derived T. This does not assume linearity of the chosen K-injective replacement functor.

Apply internalHom_localization_comparison with exactly the given continuity and cohomological lower-bound assumptions. It supplies IsIso(rho) and eta_H followed by rho = H(K,eta_L). For every n extend the latter equation by induction: postcompose both sides at n+1 with multiplication by t on H(K,UFL), use step 4 to commute H with that scalar, use the two successor equations from step 2, and cancel the invertible scalar. Thus lambda_n(H) followed by rho = H(K,lambda_n(L)). Naturality of the closed adjunction counit gives the stated evaluation equality.

Take the two presentations of step 3 and the gamma defined in the statement. Its three factors are invertible by step 5 and functoriality. Cancelling beta_L proves the first square. The beta_H leg formula, step 5, and beta_L leg formula prove the square for every n. For changes of both representatives substitute the two presentation change equations into the defining formula for gamma, apply functoriality, and cancel beta_L'. These equations prove the actual specified comparison and its representative compatibility.
